openmic_fma_filtered_subset.method: openmic-2018-metadata.csv ships a per-track `license_title` column that is a byte-identical copy of FMA raw_tracks.csv for all 20000 rows (verified 2026-09-01 by direct cross-check, 0 mismatches). Filter on it; no audio download is needed to compute the subset.
conditions: the CSV is not separately downloadable - it ships inside one 2.6 GB Zenodo tarball (md5 e4ccf187e2bb5ab2e115416e8aafe7f4)
whether CC BY-ND permits model training is an unsettled legal question, not a metadata question
licences reflect what artists declared on FMA at 2016-17 scrape time
the Zenodo archive-level CC BY 4.0 badge must never be read as clearing the audio
openmic_fma_filtered_subset.consequence: a ~2000-clip, 10 s, real-audio, commercially-filtered instrument corpus is constructible. That is enough for an evaluation set. It is thin for training.

headline: No asset in the near-term set is CLEAN_CANDIDATE for MUSICAL supervision. The only CLEAN_CANDIDATE is parirset, which is room acoustics.
